title: Reduced-Rank Generalised Dissimilarity Modelling
text: rrGDM fits Reduced Rank Generalised Dissimilarity Models (RRGDM): extension Generalised Dissimilarity Modelling (GDM) positions samples low-dimensional latent space, rather regressing pairwise dissimilarities directly pairwise environmental distances. means RRGDM can provide, one model: ordination samples predictor loadings latent space, representing composition state (like PCoA/RDA) estimates environmental predictors drive compositional turnover (like GDM), including support categorical predictors random effects (e.g., ... + (1 | group)) way separately model effects average composition versus compositional dispersion, estimated jointly latent space (see ).

title: Reduced-Rank Generalised Dissimilarity Modelling
text: can install development version rrGDM GitHub :
code: # install.packages("devtools") devtools::install_github("dhercar/rrGDM")

title: Reduced-Rank Generalised Dissimilarity Modelling
text: RRGDM places sample ii point 𝛏i\boldsymbol{\xi}_i kk-dimensional latent space, models expected pairwise dissimilarity two samples link-transformed Euclidean distance positions: g(𝔼[yij])=‖𝛏i−𝛏j‖ g\left(\mathbb{E}\left[y_{ij}\right]\right) = \lVert \boldsymbol{\xi}_i - \boldsymbol{\xi}_j \rVert RRGDM writes position along latent dimension ll linear predictor, exactly like standard regression: ξil=𝐱i𝛌l+uil,uil∼N(0,τi2) \xi_{il} = \mathbf{x}_{} \boldsymbol{\lambda}_{l} + u_{il}, \qquad u_{il} \sim N(0,\ \tau_i^2) 𝐱i\mathbf{x}_i contains predictor values sample ii, passed formula. Like modelling packages, factors dummy-coded, terms passed syntax (1|group) treated random effects. 𝛌l\boldsymbol{\lambda}_l loading describing strongly, direction, predictor influences position samples along dimension ll. uilu_{il} sample-level random effect capturing whatever structured variability (.e., variability constrained k latent variables) isn’t explained predictors. spread samples (dispersion) controlled parameter τi\tau_i, can turn modelled function external predictors via formula_sd: log⁡(τi)=κ0+𝐰i𝛋 \log(\tau_i) = \kappa_0 + \mathbf{w}_i \boldsymbol{\kappa} formula controls samples expected sit ordination space, formula_sd controls tightly expected cluster around position, estimated simultaneously. Models fit maximum likelihood via TMB, using Laplace approximation integrate random effects.

title: Reduced-Rank Generalised Dissimilarity Modelling
text: use microbialdata dataset bundled gllvm: OTU (species) table soil bacterial communities, together environmental covariates recorded sampling site.
code: library(rrGDM) library(ggplot2)  ## plotting preferences theme_set(theme_minimal()) theme_update(text = element_text(size = 11),              panel.border = element_rect(fill = 'transparent'),              panel.grid = element_blank())  set.seed(2) # Community matrix (sites x OTUs) and environmental predictors com <- gllvm::microbialdata$Y env <- gllvm::microbialdata$Xenv env$pH_s <- scale(env$pH)

title: Reduced-Rank Generalised Dissimilarity Modelling
text: fit model continuous predictor (pH_s), categorical predictor (Region), random intercept Site, entering latent composition via formula. also let dispersion depend pH via formula_sd, test whether communities become less variable pH. k number latent dimensions. 2-4 often enough. dist_method dissimilarity index computed Y (method supported vegan::vegdist()). family/link together determine raw dissimilarity (e.g. Bray-Curtis, ratio counts) relates latent distance. beta-binomial family treats dissimilarity’s numerator/denominator successes/trials, respects fact dissimilarities like ratios discrete counts, continuous [0,1][0,1] values. negative exponential link makes equal steps latent distance correspond equal proportional loss shared species (ToDo: Ref paper).
code: m1 <- rrGDM(Y = com,             X = env,             k = 2,  # 2 latent dimensions             formula = ~ pH_s + as.factor(Region) + (1|Site),             formula_sd = ~ pH_s,             family = 'beta.binomial',             link = 'negexp',             dist_method = 'bray')

what: Testing the effects of the predictors
title: Reduced-Rank Generalised Dissimilarity Modelling
text: anova() gives Wald tests predictor fitted model. row tests parameters variable (Df number parameters tested), useful factors several levels variables appear formula formula_sd. default, location (formula) dispersion (formula_sd) effects variable tested jointly. answers question variable matter ? separate = TRUE, location dispersion effects tested separate rows. answers two different questions: variable shift community composition? (location) change variable communities around position? (dispersion). Wald tests loadings can anti-conservative samples, treat p-values close threshold caution. wald_test() gives tests individual coefficient, summary() full model summary.
code: anova(m1) #>  #> ── Wald tests by variable ── #>  #> • Interaction terms included in each variable's test #> • Location and dispersion effects of the same variable tested jointly #>  #> variable  effect                 Df     Wald  Pr_Chisq #> pH_s      location + dispersion   2  138.461    <1e-06  *** #> Region    location                4   17.937     0.001  ** #>  #> Terms grouped in each test: #>   Region (location): as.factor(Region) #>  #> --- #> Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1 #> Tests on location effects can be anti-conservative with few samples. anova(m1, separate = TRUE) #> ── Wald tests by variable ── #>  #> • Interaction terms included in each variable's test #> • Location and dispersion effects tested separately #>  #> variable  effect      Df     Wald  Pr_Chisq #> pH_s      location     1  113.762    <1e-06  *** #> pH_s      dispersion   1   30.520    <1e-06  *** #> Region    location     4   17.937     0.001  ** #>  #> Terms grouped in each test: #>   Region (location): as.factor(Region) #>  #> --- #> Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1 #> Tests on location effects can be anti-conservative with few samples.

title: Reduced-Rank Generalised Dissimilarity Modelling
text: predict() can return either conditional predictions (using sample’s fitted latent position) marginal predictions (using fixed effects ignoring random effects, including sample-level deviation). Comparing observed dissimilarities useful diagnostic: Conditional fit shows well latent community composition (represented k latent dimensions) represents true variability community composition. fit poor, inference done caution. gap conditional marginal fit shows much variability community composition attributable measured predictors versus unexplained sample--sample variability.
code: par(mfrow = c(1, 2)) pred_Y <- predict(m1, conditional = TRUE)[, 3] R2_cor <-  round(cor(pred_Y, m1$Y_diss / m1$Y_den)^2,2) plot(pred_Y, m1$Y_diss / m1$Y_den,      ylab = 'observed', xlab = 'predicted',      main = paste0('conditional, Pseudo-R2: ', R2_cor)) abline(0, 1)  # median of the simulated marginal dissimilarities (column "50%") pred_Y <- predict(m1, conditional = FALSE)[, 4] R2_cor <-  round(cor(pred_Y, m1$Y_diss / m1$Y_den)^2,2) plot(pred_Y, m1$Y_diss / m1$Y_den,      ylab = 'observed', xlab = 'predicted',      main = paste0('marginal, Pseudo-R2: ', R2_cor)) abline(0, 1) par(mfrow = c(1,1))

title: Reduced-Rank Generalised Dissimilarity Modelling
text: Environmental loadings sample positions can represented latent space, possible obtain standard ordination plot environmental arrows overlaid:  ordination, worth checking much reduced kk-dimensional space distorts original dissimilarities. conditional fit already gives us idea, stress() provides another, commonly used diagnostic. returns Kruskal-style stress statistic (similar vegan::metaMDS MASS::isoMDS) comparing fitted latent distances observed dissimilarities:
code: biplot(m1, rotate = FALSE,        col_by = 'pH_s',        shape_by = 'Region') +   scale_colour_viridis_c() stress(m1) # for the rank-transformed version #> [1] 0.1176253 stress(m1, type = 'metric', scale = 'response') # for the metric version #> [1] 0.1099184

what: Visualising partial effects in ordination space
title: Reduced-Rank Generalised Dissimilarity Modelling
text: location dispersion modelled directly latent space, can visualise partial effect predictors ordination. example, represent latent coordinates three representative pH values, specifying: sim_site = TRUE: site-level random variability included via simulation N(0,τ2)N(0, \tau^2) sample_param = FALSE: parameter uncertainty included  centroids show expected community composition shifts directionally across pH gradient (effect 𝚲\boldsymbol{\Lambda}), size ellipse shows community dispersion changes pH. effects estimated jointly readable directly ordination.
code: # Creating new data X_pred <- expand.grid(   Region = as.factor(unique(gllvm::microbialdata$Xenv$Region)[1]),   Site = as.factor('Aus'),   pH_s = c(-1.5, 0, 1.5))  # Generating predictions pred_ord_2 <- predict(m1,                       newdata = X_pred,                       ordination = TRUE,                       boot = TRUE,                       sample_param = FALSE,                       sim_site = TRUE,                       n_sim = 1000)  # Plotting predicted coordinates ggplot(pred_ord_2, aes(x = L.1, y = L.2)) +   geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = 'grey') +   geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = 'grey') +   stat_ellipse(geom = 'polygon', aes(group = as.factor(pH_s)),                fill = 'white', level = 0.50) +   stat_ellipse(geom = 'path', aes(col = as.factor(pH_s)),                level = 0.95, lty = 5) +   stat_ellipse(geom = 'polygon', aes(fill = as.factor(pH_s)),                level = 0.50, alpha = 0.5) +   scale_colour_viridis_d('pH (scaled)', guide = 'none') +   scale_fill_viridis_d('pH') +   coord_equal() +   ggtitle('pH') +   xlab('LV 1') +   ylab('LV 2')

title: Wald analysis of variance table for rrGDM models — anova.rrGDM
text: object fitted model class rrGDM, fitted se = TRUE. ... used. single model can supplied (comparison several models supported). interactions Logical. Controls terms involving one variable (e.g., x:f) handled. TRUE (default), variable's test includes main-effect terms every interaction term takes part , .e., tests whether variable effect composition (dispersion) . FALSE, interaction terms omitted. Variables appear interactions omitted. separate Logical. variable can appear location model (formula) dispersion model (formula_sd). FALSE (default), tested jointly single row (effect = "location + dispersion"), accounting covariance location dispersion coefficients. TRUE, location dispersion effects variable get row .

title: Wald analysis of variance table for rrGDM models — anova.rrGDM
text: data.frame class anova_rrGDM, one row per variable (per variable effect type separate = TRUE) columns: variable: name variable. effect: "location", "dispersion"     "location + dispersion". terms: model terms grouped test. Df: degrees freedom (number free coefficients tested). Wald: Wald chi-squared statistic. Pr_Chisq: p-value. Sig: significance code.

title: Wald analysis of variance table for rrGDM models — anova.rrGDM
text: Intercepts random effects excluded. row, null hypothesis coefficients involved jointly zero. wald_test, structural zeros loadings matrix constraint == 1 excluded statistic degrees freedom. joint covariance matrix coefficients tested singular ill-conditioned (judged correlation scale; reciprocal condition number 1e-8), Wald statistic p-value row set NA warning, since test meaningful coefficients unidentified nearly collinear. Hessian optimum positive definite, function stops error. interactions = TRUE test compares model one variable dropped entirely. interactions = FALSE test variable interacts others refers effect interacting variables reference level (factors) zero (continuous predictors). wald_test, tests location effects can anti-conservative samples.

title: Wald analysis of variance table for rrGDM models — anova.rrGDM
code: set.seed(2) # simulate data n <- 25 # sites p <- 25 # species  env <- data.frame(temp = rnorm(n), moist = rnorm(n)) eta <- as.matrix(env) %*% matrix(rnorm(2 * p), 2, p) Y <- matrix(rpois(n * p, exp(1 + 0.8 * eta)), n, p,             dimnames = list(paste0("site", 1:n), paste0("sp", 1:p)))  fit <- rrGDM(Y, env, k = 2,              formula = ~ temp + moist,              family = "binomial") #> ℹ Preparing data #> ✔ Preparing data ... done #>  #> ℹ Finding initial parameters (dbRDA) #> ✔ Finding initial parameters (dbRDA) ... done #>  #> ℹ optimisation #> ℹ Start 1/1: objective = 1670.1661 #> ℹ optimisation #> ✔ optimisation ... done #>   anova(fit) #>  #> ── Wald tests by variable ── #>  #> • Interaction terms included in each variable's test #> • Location and dispersion effects of the same variable tested jointly #>  #> variable  effect    Df     Wald  Pr_Chisq #> temp      location   1  603.881    <1e-06  *** #> moist     location   2  644.000    <1e-06  *** #>  #> --- #> Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1 #> Tests on location effects can be anti-conservative with few samples. anova(fit, separate = TRUE) #> ── Wald tests by variable ── #>  #> • Interaction terms included in each variable's test #> • Location and dispersion effects tested separately #>  #> variable  effect    Df     Wald  Pr_Chisq #> temp      location   1  603.881    <1e-06  *** #> moist     location   2  644.000    <1e-06  *** #>  #> --- #> Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1 #> Tests on location effects can be anti-conservative with few samples.

title: Biplot for rrGDM objects — biplot.rrGDM
text: x fitted model class rrGDM. k Integer vector length 2 indicating latent dimensions plot. Default c(1, 2). rotate Logical indicating whether apply varimax rotation (via varimax) plotting. Default TRUE. Varimax rotates axes towards simple structure; order variance explained. get_LV, rotation estimated conditional coordinates (L), whatever type plotted. type Character string: either 'conditional' (site scores including sample-level error, L) 'marginal' (site scores determined environmental loadings , L_m). Default 'conditional'. col_by Optional character string naming variable x$X used colour points. Ignored add_points = FALSE. shape_by Optional character string naming variable x$X used shape points. Ignored add_points = FALSE. add_points Logical indicating whether add default sample points layer via ggplot2::geom_point(). Default TRUE. Set FALSE omit layer entirely add fully custom one instead. returned plot's default data already contains rotated latent coordinates together columns used fit model, biplot(model, add_points = FALSE) + ggplot2::geom_point(ggplot2::aes(fill = pH), shape = 21) works directly, control aesthetics, shapes, legends. env_load Logical indicating whether add environmental loadings arrows. Default TRUE. species_cor Logical indicating whether add species labels positioned (Spearman) correlation plotted latent axis. Default FALSE. species_cor_n Optional integer. species_cor = TRUE, species_cor_n species strongest correlation labelled. Useful community matrix hundreds thousands species. Default 20. Set NULL label species. env_load_scale Numeric scale factor applied environmental loading arrows. Default 1. sp_load_scale Numeric scale factor applied species-correlation labels. Default 1. text_size Numeric text size used species labels. Default 3. compare Logical indicating whether overlay marginal scores top conditional scores, connected segment. valid type = 'conditional'. Default FALSE. ... Currently unused.

Note: Distances between centroids are not equivalent to the expected #>   (average) distances or dissimilarities between samples, which can be much #>   larger. #> • To calculate expected dissimilarities between samples, set `boot = TRUE` and #>   `sim_site = TRUE`. head(pred) #>   s1 s2      dist #> 1  1  2 0.8835308 #> 2  1  3 0.8790634 #> 3  1  4 0.8763481 #> 4  1  5 0.8586837 #> 5  1  6 0.8996577 #> 6  1  7 0.8921820  # Predict ordination coordinates pred_ord <- predict(fit,                     ordination = TRUE, # latent positions                     conditional = TRUE)  head(pred_ord) #>           L.1        L.2 sample        temp      moist #> 1 -0.80450922 -1.6343846      1 -0.89691455 -2.4517064 #> 2  0.05922709  0.2442293      2  0.18484918  0.4772373 #> 3  0.80887279 -0.5117871      3  1.58784533 -0.5965582 #> 4 -0.81997210  0.5303289      4 -1.13037567  0.7922033 #> 5 -0.14375128  0.2680057      5 -0.08025176  0.2896367 #> 6  0.12394223  0.4742975      6  0.13242028  0.7389386 plot(pred_ord[,c(1,2)])   # with newdata new <- data.frame(temp = c(-1, 0, 1), moist = c(0, 0, 0)) pred_new <- predict(fit, newdata = new) head(pred_new) #>   s1 s2      2.5%       50%     97.5% #> 1  1  2 0.2358371 0.4706934 0.6278474 #> 2  1  3 0.5744552 0.7027264 0.7928866 #> 3  2  3 0.2371924 0.4687820 0.6363789  # Predict position in ordination pred_new_ord <- predict(fit,                         newdata = new,                         ordination = TRUE,                         n_sim = 500)  # Visualise sample-level variability plot(pred_new_ord$L.1,      pred_new_ord$L.2,      xlab = 'L1',      ylab = 'L2',      asp = 1,      col = c('blue', 'grey', 'red')[as.numeric(as.factor(pred_new_ord$temp))])

text: Y matrix data frame containing response variable (usually species abundance matrix). X data frame containing predictor variables. k integer specifying number latent variables used model. Default 2. binary Logical indicating whether response variable treated binary (e.g., presence-absence). Default FALSE. formula Formula specifying model fitted. formula_sd Formula specifying model dispersion parameter. Default ~1 (intercept ). dist_method character string specifying distance method used (e.g., "euclidean", "bray"). Default "bray". scale_diss numeric vector length two indicating new scale dissimilarities. Useful distributions bounded 0 1 (e.g., beta family). Ignored, warning, "binomial" "beta.binomial" families. family character string specifying family response variable: "gaussian", "binomial", "beta" "beta.binomial". Default "gaussian". link Character string specifying link function used: "identity", "negexp" "neggaus". Default 'identity' Gaussian distribution, 'negexp' beta binomial distributions. se Logical indicating whether calculate standard errors (TRUE) (FALSE). Default TRUE. sample_error Logical. TRUE, includes site-level random effects account variation explained predictors. Default TRUE. constraint Integer. Specifies identifiability constraints. 0: constraint; 1: Constraint applied environmental loadings matrix (\(\Lambda\)); 2: Constraint applied site random effects matrix (U). Default 1. trans Function used transform response matrix computing dissimilarities (e.g., log, sqrt). Default transformation. sparse Optional object class sparse_diss (see sparse_diss). supplied, model fitted using pairs samples listed sparse$edges, instead pairs. must created samples Y. Default NULL (pairs). seed integer passed set.seed() start fit, changes state R's random number generator. Default NULL (seed set). init_jitter Numeric. Standard deviation Gaussian noise added starting values every start first. used n_starts > 1. Default 0.1. n_starts Integer. Number optimisation starts. first start uses values init_method (start_fit); start adds Gaussian noise (SD init_jitter) best solution far (previous_best = TRUE) initial values (FALSE). one start, fits converged positive-definite Hessian eligible final fit. Default 1. previous_best Logical. Controls jitter multiple starts first applied. TRUE (default), start jitters around best solution found far (perturb--reoptimise). FALSE, every start jitters around initial values (init_method), starts depend earlier fits. relevant n_starts > 1. init_method character string specifying method used obtain initial values optimisation. Currently, 'PCOA' 'dbRDA' available; NULL starts small random values. Default 'dbRDA'. Ignored start_fit supplied. start_fit Optional fitted rrGDM model used initialise optimisation (e.g., fast sparse fit refitting pairs). must samples, k, family, link, constraint, predictors random-effect structure new model; set pairs (sparse) may differ. supplied, init_method ignored. Default NULL. trace Logical. TRUE, TMB prints optimisation progress objective start reported. Default FALSE. control list control parameters passed nlminb. iter.max defaults 1000.

what: Calculate Stress for a fitted rrGDM model — stress
title: Calculate Stress for a fitted rrGDM model — stress
text: Computes goodness--fit "stress" statistic fitted rrGDM object, comparing observed dissimilarities used fit model model-implied quantity computed conditional latent coordinates (.e., including sample-level errors): either raw Euclidean distance fitted latent positions (scale = "link"), inverse-link-transformed expected dissimilarity (scale = "response"). type = "nonmetric", Kruskal's stress-1, $$Stress = \sqrt{\frac{\sum (\hat{d} - D)^2}{\sum D^2}}$$ \(D\) chosen model-implied quantity \(\hat{d}\) ("disparities") isotonic (monotone) regression \(D\) observed dissimilarities. type = "metric", observed model-implied dissimilarities compared directly, regression step: $$Stress = \sqrt{\frac{\sum (y_{ij} - \hat{y}_{ij})^2}{\sum y_{ij}^2}}$$ \(y_{ij}\) observed dissimilarities \(\hat{y}_{ij}\) model-implied ones. allow linear recalibration, also penalises poorly calibrated link. directly comparable stress reported NMDS software. Stress returned proportion 0 (best) 1 (worst) bounded dissimilarities.
